Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.metaDescription: Kvaterka.by's platform rules and the current status of its legal documents.
Terms.lede: Below is how the platform actually works. A formal agreement hasn't been drafted yet — and we say so plainly instead of hiding it behind generic wording.

note.p1Rich: Document in progress. The terms of service need to be drafted by a lawyer practicing in Belarus. Until that happens, we won't publish text that looks like a contract but isn't one. This is a deliberate choice: invented legal wording is more dangerous than having none.
note.p2: Until an agreement exists, the platform runs on the rules described on this page. They're built into the software itself and applied the same way to everyone.

what.heading: What the platform does
what.body: Kvaterka is a place where a host publishes a listing, a tenant finds it, asks questions, sends a request, and leaves a review after the stay. The platform keeps the messages, confirmations, and dispute decisions.

not.heading: What the platform doesn't do
not.item1Rich: Isn't a party to your deal. The rental agreement is between the two of you. Kvaterka isn't a party to it.
not.item2Rich: Doesn't take rent or a deposit. You pay the rent to each other directly.
not.item3Rich: Doesn't guarantee the condition of the property. Moderator review of a listing is a review of the listing, not of the flat.

fee.heading: Platform fee
fee.bodyRich: The host is charged 5% after a completed stay confirmed by both sides. <link>How the fee is calculated</link>.

rules.heading: Rules the platform enforces itself
rules.item1: Contact details aren't shared until a booking is confirmed — this protects both sides.
rules.item2: A review can only be left after a stay has taken place, one from each side.
rules.item3: Both sides' reviews are published at the same time.
rules.item4: Financial records and the action log are immutable, including for staff.
rules.item5: A listing goes through moderation before it's published.

disputes.heading: Disputes
disputes.body: A dispute is opened from the booking card. A platform staff member decides it based on the message history and the check-in/check-out marks. The decision is logged and can't be rewritten after the fact.

Terms.footerRich: What happens to your data — <privacyLink>on a separate page</privacyLink>. Questions — <supportLink>contact support</supportLink>.
